history.summary: The only major temple where Rama is worshipped as a KING, not as a deity, with daily royal protocol including a guard of honour. Per legend, Queen Ganesh Kunwar (Ganeshkuwari), wife of Bundela king Madhukar Shah, brought an idol of Rama from Ayodhya; Rama's condition was that he would stay wherever the idol was first set down. The queen rested it in her palace kitchen, and when the grand Chaturbhuj Temple (RELATED RECORD: seq 1814) built to enshrine it was finished, the idol would not move — so the palace itself became the Ram Raja Temple. The seated Rama idol shows only the left leg crossed in padmasana; devotees seek darshan of the left big toe, believed to grant wishes. Timings vary by Hindu calendar season. Note: older sources list the district as Tikamgarh; Orchha moved to Niwari district (created 2018).

name: Ram Raja Temple
town_description: Orchha is a historic town in Niwari district (older sources say Tikamgarh) on the Betwa river, founded in 1531 by Rudra Pratap Singh as the capital of the Bundela Rajputs. It holds the Orchha Fort complex, Jahangir Mahal and Rani Mahal palaces, the Chaturbhuj temple, and the famous riverfront cenotaphs (chhatris) of the Bundela rulers. It lies about 15 km from Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh, its main railhead.

travel.road: On SH-37/NH-39 network; regular buses and taxis from Jhansi, Gwalior and Bhopal
